By the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence dated 28.08.2023 passed in Special Criminal Case No. H-56/2022 by the court of learned Special Judge (POCSO Act) Mahasamund, District - Mahasamund Chhattisgarh the appellant Yashwant Jangade has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 363, 366 of the Indian Penal Code (in short 'the IPC') and Section 6 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for five years with fine of Rs. 1,000/-, in default of payment of fine further R.I for one month, to undergo R.I. for seven years with fine of Rs. 2,000/-, in default of payment of fine further R.I for two months, to undergo R.I. for twenty years with fine of Rs. 10,000/-, in default of payment of fine further R.I for six months.

sentences.text: Conviction of the appellant is also under Sections 376(2)(<+) of IPC but no separate sentence has been awarded under this Section because the sentence for offence of Section 6 of POCSO Act has been awarded.
There is direction to run all the jail sentences concurrently.

Heard Mr. K.S. Kurrey, learned counsel for the appellant and Mr. Pawan Kesharwani, learned panel lawyer for the State/respondent on the instant application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail (IA No. 1 of 2023) filed by appellant Yashwant Jangade.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the present case and there is no evidence on record to connect the appellant with commission of the offence.
He further submits that the prosecutrix was a consenting party and it is a case of elopement not of taking away enticing or abduction.
There are many contradiction and omissions in the statement of the prosecution witness.

He further submits that the appellant was on bail during trail and he is in jail since 28.08.2023 the appeal is likely to take some time for its conclusion, hence the appellant has filed the instant application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
Learned counsel for the State/respondent would oppose the application.

It was argued by Mr.
Pawan Kesharwani, learned panel lawyer that there is ample evidence on record to connect the appellant with commission of the offence.
He further submits that at the time of incident victim was a minor girl and MLC report is also positive.
He further submits that notice has been served and findings arrived at by the learned trial Court is just and proper.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records of the Court below.
Considering the material available in record, we are inclined to allow the application for grant of bail.
Accordingly, the substantive jail sentence awarded to appellant Yashwant Jangade by the learned trial Court is hereby suspended.
He shall be released on bail on his executing bail bond to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 06.02.2024.

He shall thereafter, appear before the concerned trial Court on a date to be given by the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given to him by the said Court, interval being not less than 6 months, till fnal disposal of this appeal.
Consequently, I.A. No. 1 of 2023 fled by appellant Yashwant Jangade is allowed.

It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only confned for disposal of aforesaid I.A. fled in this appeal and it shall not be construed as an expression of opinion of this Court on the merits of the matter.
List this matter for fnal hearing.
 Sd/- Sd/-
 (Ravindra Kumar Agrawal) (Ramesh Sinha)
